title: Lusitanus Hall dances and Dave Perkins, the trombonist who passed for white
summary: After locating Lusitanus Hall, Laine praises Perkins as his first reader, playing lead on trombone, and says Perkins was a light-skinned man passing for white.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Fine old dance. Did you ever play the Lusitanus Hall? Oh my God. Yeah. Where was that at?
Huh? Where was that at? The Lusitanus on Dauphine? Mm-hmm. Yeah.

Yeah. Dauphine, what was the other street that it was on? Dauphine and Lusitanus. Dauphine near what? Near Lusitanus? Lusitanus. Lusitanus. Wasn't it? No. On Dauphine and Lusitanus? Yeah, that's right. Well, that's right near Knob's Bar. Yeah, next to the police station. Where, Lusitanus? Lusitanus. Yeah. That's where we used to be. On Lusitanus. Yeah. That's where we used to be.

That's the way Perkins learned us how to play. Oh, with respect to you, bumps you the rat tail. I forgot the name. I can't figure that. He pumped away with his trombones, that damn pursuing. Boy, he turned the house down.

What kind of style did he play? How would he play? What kind of trombone would he play? How did he sound? What was it like? Pretty good. Yeah, but would he go? No, no. He played the whole melody. Oh, played the whole melody.
Yes, sir. Oh, Perkins was a musician. He carried the lead, huh? Huh? He carried the lead.
Yeah, yeah, carried the lead. Yeah. Mm-hmm. Now, was that the first real musician you had ever been around, Dave Perkins? The first one ever I have been.
You mixed up with your... I see. First one.
Reader. Musicians are readers, you see.

Readers. The first reader, I see. Yeah. And mind you, it turned out that this Dave Perkins was a colored man, too. Is that right? Yeah. But he was passing for white. Is that right? Oh, yes. Uh-huh. He was going to marry a white girl. Oh. In my neighborhood. I see. And somebody put her next to it. Something. Yeah.
Ask him what color hair he had.

What color hair did he have? Straight hair. Straight black? Blonde. Blonde hair. Yeah, he was blonde. Fair as a lily. With blue eyes. Fair as a lily. Blue eyes? Yes. Yes. And let me tell you one thing about that guy. That guy was a good drug clerk. Is that right? Yes, sir.
